assessment_summary:
Proof attempt:
1. Assume X_n converges to X in distribution.
2. By definition, F_{X_n}(t) -> F_X(t) at all continuity points t of F_X.
3. This implies that the joint distribution of (X_n, X) concentrates on the diagonal x = y.

Evaluation:
Step 3 is flawed. Convergence in distribution only concerns the marginal distributions of X_n and X. It does not place any restrictions on their joint distribution that would force them to be close in probability. The proof attempt fails here.
counterexample: Let X ~ N(0,1) and X_n = -X for all n. X_n and X have the same distribution, so X_n trivially converges to X in distribution. However, |X_n - X| = |-X - X| = 2|X|. For any eps > 0, P(|X_n - X| > eps) = P(|X| > eps/2) > 0. This probability does not converge to 0 as n -> infinity, so X_n does not converge to X in probability.
